cells.tense: You are holding what you made, and the holding is easy today.
cells.ask: Set it down for one hour and pick it up again; notice whether your hands know the difference.
cells.core:
When this is going well, you can move through a thing that isn't clear yet without needing the whole road lit. You take the next step on the light you have, and the next one shows up when you get there. That is the whole skill, and you have it. What you began has finished becoming something, and you are carrying it without strain — the weight is real, and your grip on it is light. You don't need the ending mapped to keep walking toward it.

One hour with it set down costs you nothing and tells you everything. Put it where you can see it, or where nobody can, and watch what your hands do without it. What you're actually holding will make itself known, and you'll pick it up again knowing more than you did.

cells.tense: You are living past the next step, in a finish line you can't reach from here.
cells.ask: Look at one thing exactly as it is right now, with nothing about what it will become attached, and say what you actually see.
cells.core:
When this is going well, uncertainty is workable — you have enough light for the next step and you trust that the step after it will come into view. You don't force the picture to be whole before you move. Right now you're out ahead of where you stand, bracing against an ending that hasn't arrived, and the bracing is eating the walking. You wanted to carry the finished thing all at once, so the next step reads as stalling. The pressure isn't coming from the road. It's coming from the road you're picturing.

What opens this back up is a plain look at what's in front of you — no verdicts, no previews of what it turns into. See the one thing beside you only as it appears, and let that be enough to take you forward.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing toward the end and skipping the ground under you.

cells.tense: You stopped at a step you already took, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Let one person tell you about something they're carrying, and hear it without deciding anything about it.
cells.core:
When this is going well, you walk into not-knowing on purpose. You move with a partial view, let the path show itself as you go, and it does. The thing you built is still standing, and you've gone quiet beside it. You wait for a full picture before the next move, and the waiting has turned into standing still. The light hasn't gone out. You've stopped walking by it.

What's missing isn't effort — pushing harder at this won't do it. What's missing is the willingness to be reached: to let something in before it's been sorted and let it work on you a while. Sit with one piece of what someone else is carrying and leave it unjudged.

cells.tense: You are already moving through what isn't clear yet, and calling it drift.
cells.ask: Say "I chose this" about one place you're standing in that you've been calling where you ended up.
cells.core:
When this is going well, you can hold a direction without seeing the whole of it — you pick a way forward, adjust as the ground changes, and let the picture fill in behind you. You are doing that already. You steer through uncertainty every day, and you describe it as being carried along. The navigating is real. The credit isn't going where it belongs.

Nothing here needs inventing, and nothing needs to be bigger than it is. Take one thing you built and say plainly that you made the choices inside it — the small ones count — and let that claim rest on the one who made them.
